question: Who was India’s 12th Prime Minister?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Inder Kumar Gujral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Inder Kumar Gujral** was the 12th Prime Minister of India, serving from April 1997 to March 1998.
 
• He succeeded H. D. Deve Gowda and was succeeded by Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
 
• Gujral was a member of the Janata Dal party during his tenure as Prime Minister.
 
• He is well-known for the "Gujral Doctrine," a set of five principles to guide India's foreign policy towards its neighbors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Ministers of India**

 
 
• The Prime Minister of India is the head of the government and exercises most executive powers.
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India and must be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, the two houses of India's Parliament.
 
• The first Prime Minister of India was Jawaharlal Nehru, who took office on August 15, 1947, following India’s independence from British rule.
 
• As of 2023, Narendra Modi is the current and 15th Prime Minister of India, having taken office on May 26, 2014.
 
 
 
• **Janata Dal**
 
 
• Janata Dal was an Indian political party that was formed in 1988.
 
• The party played a significant role in Indian politics during the late 1980s and 1990s.
 
• It emerged from the merger of various opposition parties to form a united front against the Indian National Congress.
 
• Janata Dal members included several former Prime Ministers, such as V. P. Singh, H. D. Deve Gowda, and Inder Kumar Gujral.
 
 
 
• **Gujral Doctrine**
 
 
• The Gujral Doctrine is a set of five principles to guide the conduct of India’s foreign relations with its immediate neighbors.
 
• It was formulated by Inder Kumar Gujral during his tenure as the Minister of External Affairs and later as Prime Minister.
 
• The doctrine emphasizes unilateral accommodation and goodwill towards India's smaller neighbors without expecting reciprocity.
 
• It aimed to foster better relations and ensure regional peace and stability.
